summary: Present the subject as a deliberately crafted small object using a readable base, tactile parts and selective oversizing.
objective: The base and part treatment convey the intended miniature reading, and focus effects never hide the currently selected component.
intent_signals: Present the scene as a toy miniature
Emphasize tactile parts and a crafted display base
example_prompts: Build a collectible miniature village on a crafted base with individually readable doors.

principles: Present the subject as a deliberately crafted small object using a readable base, tactile parts and selective oversizing.
implementation: Thicken fragile-looking parts for the imagined toy design, separate assembly seams and keep one consistent miniature scale cue.
Use clean painted finishes, small wear accents and a studio key; shallow-focus treatment is optional and should not obscure inspection.
Use a tabletop-height orbit or slightly elevated view, then offer close inspection; restrained mechanical or playful motion can reinforce the crafted object.
Thicken any part thinner than 1.5 mm at true scale to 2.5-3 mm, and keep one repeated scale cue in every view (a 2.0 m door at 1:24 is 83 mm).
Shoot from 25-45 degrees above the base at 0.4-1.2 m orbit distance; a 55 mm-equivalent lens at f/2.8 gives a 60-90 mm sharp band, which is the actual miniature cue.
observable_checks: The base and part treatment convey the intended miniature reading, and focus effects never hide the currently selected component.

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at renderer.toneMappingExposure 1.05; re-tune intensities and fog density under a different tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with low-poly, clay or glass accents; toy appearance does not change the units of an underlying factual model.

defaults.rationale: The miniature read comes from viewing geometry, not from the object: a high 35 degree down-pitch at 0.4-1.6 m with a 70 mm depth-of-field band mimics a macro lens over a tabletop, which is why the orbit distances are short and the polar range stays above the object. Lighting is product-clean at 2.5:1 with a 0.9 rim so no part disappears during inspection, and the depth-of-field band is explicitly forbidden from blurring the currently selected component.

values.value_structure: 30/50/20 dark/mid/light; the display base stays one stop under the object
values.saturation_rule: base and backdrop <= 30% saturation; the toy body up to 75%

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 2.5:1 - product-clean, no part hidden in a mystery shadow

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: injection-moulded plastic 0.35, matte paint 0.6, rubber 0.7; 0.2 mm parting-line bevel and a 3% edge-wear mask on the accent colour

post.dof: focus on the hero part, 70 mm sharp band at f/2.8 equivalent; never narrow enough to blur the selected component

values.signature_technique: a 35 degree down-angle at 0.4-1.6 m paired with a 70 mm depth-of-field band, so the eye reads the subject as small rather than as a scaled building
never: depth of field that blurs the selected part
